# ISO 27001 Certification Roadmap for Your Firm

## Context assumptions

| Factor | Your situation | Implication |
|---|---|---|
| Size | 120 employees | Small-medium ISMS scope; lean documentation is fine |
| Sector | Financial services | Regulator expectations (likely FCA, SEC, or similar) will reinforce many controls; auditors will expect mature controls around data classification, access, and continuity |
| Infrastructure | Hybrid (Azure + on-prem) | Cloud-specific controls matter (5.23 Cloud services); shared responsibility model must be documented |
| SOC | Outsourced | Supplier management controls are critical; you need evidence the SOC meets your requirements |
| ITIL maturity | Partial (incident, change) | Good start — these map directly to key Annex A controls; gaps likely in config management, service continuity, and monitoring |
| MFA | Remote access only | Auditors will ask why not internally and for privileged accounts |
| Asset inventory | Incomplete | This is a **blocker** — almost every control domain depends on knowing what you're protecting |
| ISMS | None formal | Clauses 4–10 documentation needed from scratch |
| Timeline | ~6 months | Aggressive but achievable if you start the mandatory clauses and high-priority controls immediately |

---

**Timing**: Last week of Month 5 or first week of Month 6

The Stage 1 audit is a **documentation review**. The auditor will:

1. Review ISMS documentation for completeness and conformity to Clauses 4–10
2. Review the SoA and risk assessment/treatment
3. Assess readiness for Stage 2
4. Identify any areas of concern (not formal NCs at Stage 1, but noted gaps will block Stage 2)
5. Confirm the Stage 2 audit plan and scope

**You must have**: All mandatory documented information, a functioning ISMS, and evidence that the PDCA cycle has turned at least once (risk assessment → controls → internal audit → management review → improvement).
